findings.title: New PR-comment template drops the culprit/subtitle and truncates titles
findings.body: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` no longer includes the issue culprit/subtitle. `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` also truncates titles to 50 chars with `...`. The PR comment now carries less context than before, and nothing in the PR description mentions the change. The template also ends in `\n`, and each item is joined with `\n`, so every entry is followed by a blank line. That produces separate paragraphs instead of a tight list, and trailing blank lines in the GitLab body. The tests were rewritten to match this output.

findings.title: get_environment_info triggers an extra event fetch per issue
findings.body: For every issue in the comment, `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` and then `get_environment()`. That is an extra nodestore/Snuba lookup per issue, up to 5, inside the comment task. The broad `except Exception` swallows failures and logs only at info level. The helper also logs under the key `no-environment` even when the cause is a real error.

findings.title: Static method references PRCommentWorkflow instead of the defining class
findings.body: `get_merged_pr_single_issue_template` is a `@staticmethod` on `CommitContextIntegration`, but it calls `PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title`. `_truncate_title` is defined on `CommitContextIntegration`, not on `PRCommentWorkflow`. If `PRCommentWorkflow` is a different class, as its name suggests, this raises AttributeError. The call should reference `CommitContextIntegration`.

findings.title: Default autofix automation tuning silently changed from "low" to "off"
findings.body: `DEFAULT_AUTOFIX_AUTOMATION_TUNING_DEFAULT` and the project option default both change from `low` to `off`. Projects that never set this option change behavior: autofix automation stops running for them. The change is not mentioned in the PR description, and it is unrelated to the replay bulk-delete theme.

findings.title: Applied migrations rewritten into no-ops
findings.body: Migrations 0917 and 0920 are replaced with no-ops, and the 0917 test is deleted. The comment claims they never ran. Any environment that already applied the originals, or any self-hosted install, silently loses that conversion. The comment points to a `0921_..._rerevised` migration, but that file is not part of this change, so the data fix may not exist. Rewriting history is also risky for migration state.

findings.title: Unauthenticated endpoint logs full request body and raw invalid payloads
findings.body: The endpoint has `permission_classes = ()`. It logs the entire `request.data` at info level on every request, and logs the raw invalid data at warning level. Anonymous clients can inject arbitrarily large or sensitive content into logs. No batch size or list length limit is enforced either.

findings.title: age/timestamp validators use truthiness, so a value of 0 is accepted alongside the other field
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` and `validate_age` check `self.initial_data.get(...)` for truthiness. `age: 0` or `timestamp: 0` therefore passes the mutual-exclusion check. The two specs can be mixed, and a report with neither field is also accepted. The check should use `is not None` or key presence. If exactly one of the two is required, add that requirement.

findings.title: Error events zipped with nodestore result by position, and timestamp may be a string
findings.body: `zip(error_ids, events.values())` assumes `get_multi` returns values in the same order as the requested IDs. The dict is keyed by node ID, and any missing node is dropped from the result, so the IDs and values can misalign. Event IDs get attached to the wrong data. In addition, nodestore `timestamp` is a float in normal events but is not validated. `error_events.sort` and the `<` comparison will raise on bad types.

findings.title: Extra Snuba and nodestore queries on every request, even for pagination
findings.body: Each GET runs `query_replay_instance` against Snuba and a nodestore multi-get. This happens outside the paginator and is repeated for every page request. `error_events` is also sorted in place inside `get_request_data`, which mutates a list shared across the `on_results` call. The error context should be fetched once and the in-place mutation avoided.

findings.title: Analytics recorded before the feature flag check
findings.body: `analytics.record` runs before `features.has(...)`. Orgs without the feature, whose request then returns 404, still emit `preprod_artifact.api.assemble` events. This inflates the metric. It also uses `request.user.id`, which may be None or missing for org-token auth. The event could be recorded after the feature check.

findings.title: Owner field is not validated against the organization
findings.body: `ActorField` is added to the validator, but the validator does not check that the owner belongs to the organization. The new tests (`test_owner_not_in_organization`, `test_invalid_owner`) assert a 400 for an owner from another org. Nothing in this diff enforces that, so those tests may fail, and a cross-org owner may be accepted. Add an explicit `validate_owner`.

findings.title: New hard processing deadlines on webhook delivery tasks
findings.body: The deadlines are 30s for the scheduler, 300s for `drain_mailbox`, and 120s for `drain_mailbox_parallel`. They are new and unexplained. Draining a mailbox with slow or retrying destinations can exceed them, and the task is then killed and retried mid-delivery. This risks duplicate webhook delivery.

findings.title: TableWidgetVisualization rendered with empty placeholder data behind feature flag
findings.body: When `use-table-widget-visualization` is enabled, `TableWidgetVisualization` is rendered with `columns={[]}` and empty `tableData`. The real `result.data` and `meta` are never passed. Every table widget therefore renders blank for orgs with the flag, and the loading state is ignored.

findings.title: Optional chaining on a required prop, then unguarded access
findings.body: `tableData?.meta.fields` is used even though `tableData` is a required prop. If `tableData` were undefined, `.meta` would still throw, so the optional chaining protects nothing. `renderDefaultHeadCell` also passes `column.name` to `fieldAlignment` where a field key is expected. When `columns` supplies a custom display name, alignment is computed from the display name instead.

findings.title: Query key and caching behavior changed: staleTime and refetch settings dropped, key omits org
findings.body: The hook moves from `useApiQuery` to a raw `useQuery`. The query key `['use-trace-item-attribute-keys', queryOptions]` does not include the organization slug. Two orgs with identical filters can share a cache entry. The previous `staleTime: 0`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` and `retry: false` options are dropped, so defaults now apply (window-focus refetch, retries). `isLoading` is now mapped to `isFetching`, which flickers on background refetches. The environment filter is also removed from the request.

findings.title: isVisualize now requires `yAxis` string, breaking detection of JSON-form visualizes
findings.body: The `isVisualize` check changed from `yAxes` to `yAxis`. Plain `BaseVisualize` objects, such as the output of `toJSON()`, are no longer recognized. The same applies to saved-query data or any caller still passing `{yAxes: [...]}`. The `findAllFieldRefs` fix works around this by switching to `isBaseVisualize`, but other call sites may regress. A multi-yAxes `BaseVisualize` is also now silently expanded into several charts (`fromJSON` now returns an array), which changes saved-query and URL behavior.

findings.title: Analytics event name changed with no registration for the old name
findings.body: `replay.view_html` becomes `replay.view-html` here. This is consistent with `replayAnalyticsEvents`, but the event name change breaks any downstream dashboards or queries on the old name. Mention it, or keep the old name.
